summary: R. Gayathri is an Indologist. She studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.

R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. Educated at Columbia and the LSE, he worked for newspapers, Guaranty Trust Company (1928–1934), and J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963), serving on the ACLS Executive Committee in 1951.

R. H. Blyth (1898–1964) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of London. He held academic posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1946–1947).
R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian who studied at Balliol College, Oxford. He held posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1913–1949).
R. N. Gadre was an Indologist. In 1959, he is attested as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was an Indology scholar who earned a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He held posts at Presidency College, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

R. Venkatraman is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, and was attested there as Reader in 1990.
Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a philosopher who studied at University College London (~1878–1880). He founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.
Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York. She held a post as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool around 2017.

Rachel H. Pang specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia and was attested in 2019 as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College.

Rachelle M. Scott is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985) was an Indologist and historian educated at Patna University. He headed history at Ganesh Dutt College (1946), served as principal of Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and taught history at Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University (1974–1984).

Radha Kumud Mukherjee (1884–1963) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1917) and Maharaja's College, University of Mysore (~1917–1921).

Radhika Herzberger (born 1938) works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal (~1976–1982) and became Director of Rishi Valley School around 1982.

Rafal Stepien is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure, and held appointments at Wadham College, Oxford (2012–2013) and Harvard University (2015).
Rafał Felbur is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He was a PhD candidate at Stanford University under Paul Harrison, having also studied under John R. McRae and Luis O. Gómez.
Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome from approximately 1976 to 2020.
Raffaello Orlando is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University in 1981 under the supervision of Denis Twitchett.

Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was an Indologist educated at University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He headed Sanskrit at Sanatan Dharma College (~1931–1946) and founded the International Academy of Indian Culture, serving as its director in 1934.
